rule:
The clear width of the staircase must be at least 1 m.

Regulatory text (the authoritative clauses - use them to interpret the requirement and its applicability; you must still work out how to measure it from the IFC geometry):
BCA Approved Document (Acceptable Solutions) V7.08 - applicability:
E.2.1 A staircase (including a flight of 2 steps or more) shall provide a safe and suitable passage for movement of people.
E.2.2 A staircase must have - ... (c) sufficient width, tread and riser to avoid injury; ...
E.2.4 The requirements in paragraph E.2.2(b) and (c) do not apply to a staircase located in any of the following rooms or spaces:
  (a) any equipment or plant room;
  (b) any production area of an industrial building;
  (c) any attic that - (ii) does not exceed an area of 10 square metres; and (iii) is in a residential building;
  (d) any house built for the owner's own use.

BCA Approved Document (Acceptable Solutions) — E.3.3 Width of staircase:
E.3.3.1 The clear width of every staircase shall not be less than 1000 mm.
Note: If the projection of the handrail into the clear width does NOT exceed 80 mm on each side of the staircase, the width is measured from:
  (a) the finished surfaces of the walls, if the staircase is enclosed on both sides by walls only; or
  (b) the finished surface of the wall and the inner side of the balustrade, if the staircase has a wall on one side and a balustrade on the other; or
  (c) the inner sides of the balustrades if the staircase has balustrades on both sides.
If the projection of the handrail into the clear width EXCEEDS 80 mm on one or more side, the clear width is measured from:
  (a) the finished surface of the wall and the inner side of the handrail, if the staircase has a wall on one side and a handrail on the other; or
  (b) the inner sides of the handrails if the staircase has handrails on both sides.
(E.3.2.1: no projection other than handrails is allowed into the staircase space within 2.0 m of the landing or pitch line.)

Benchmark labelling policy: Label every IfcStair. Use NA for a staircase exempt under E.2.1 or E.2.4. Use MANUAL_CHECK for a staircase located in a cinema, theatre or amphitheatre space, or whose stair shape type is not defined in the model (IfcStair PredefinedType NOTDEFINED); the reference checker does not assess these automatically. Measure the clear width from walls or other solid elements, or from the edge of the stair flight where there is none; a railing reduces the width only where it projects more than 80 mm inside that line, and a railing within the flight divides it so that the narrowest part counts. This policy comes from the reference checker, not from the regulation text.

Report the GlobalId of every element (modelled as IfcStair) that does NOT satisfy this requirement.
notes: Full population of 59 IfcStair: {'FAIL': 23, 'MANUAL_CHECK': 4, 'NA': 6, 'PASS': 26}. Expert workbook labels with independent IFC applicability and clear-width evidence. The 49-stair subset case remains unchanged.

reference.status: expert workbook labels cross-checked against IFC evidence with 2 recorded adjudications; not independent expert certification
reference.width_convention: Stated in the rule text: clear width between walls/solids or flight edges; railings reduce the width only where they project more than 80 mm; a railing within the flight divides it and the narrowest lane counts. Independent measurement: 40 of 49 expert widths within 10 mm, 48 of 49 outcomes agree.
reference.limitations: The stated convention differs from a strict reading measured from each balustrade's own inner side, which would change the outcome for the listed IDs. Industrial building use and residential-unit status are not recorded in the IFC; the E.2.4 and manual-check conditions rely on space names, storey names and occupancy properties. Geometry checks corroborate the workbook; they are not independent expert certification.
